item.title: More Marines are headed to Middle East as Iran war reaches the 3-week mark
item.summary: The USS Boxer group of three ships, carrying thousands of Marines from the 11the Marine Expeditionary Unit, has left California and will reach the Persian Gulf in about three weeks, NPR has confirmed.

item.title: Why is the 'Bachelorette' canceled? A guide to the Taylor Frankie Paul controversy
item.summary: Taylor Frankie Paul rose to fame on The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, then filmed a season of The Bachelorette. But it won't air as planned because of resurfaced domestic violence allegations.

item.title: With 'Arirang,' BTS returns to a K-pop moment of its own making
item.summary: Four years ago, the boy band went silent — but not before setting off a chain reaction that would reshape the pop market, conquer the Grammys and prime the world for an inevitable comeback.

item.title: Palestinians celebrate Eid in Gaza, making the most of a fragile ceasefire
item.summary: The ceasefire, in effect for the past six months, has brought some reprieve to Palestinians in Gaza despite continued hardship, displacement and Israeli restrictions on aid.

item.title: He's one reason why aid cuts weren't as dire for the HIV population as predicted
item.summary: Harerimana Ismail of Uganda is a community health worker who checks on kids with HIV. He lost his salary after the Trump administration's aid cuts but he keeps doing his job.

item.title: Ryan Gosling and a cute alien team up to save humanity in 'Project Hail Mary'
item.summary: The story is fundamentally hopeful, just like Andy Weir's The Martian.

item.title: From mall to torture site: Venezuela debates El Helicoide prison's future
item.summary: Once a futuristic shopping mall, El Helicoide became one of Venezuela's most feared prisons. Now, as the country changes, so does its fate — erase it, rebuild it, or remember what happened inside.

item.title: Epstein's former attorney testifies he had 'no knowledge whatsoever' of crimes
item.summary: Darren Indyke, longtime attorney for Jeffrey Epstein, testified he "did not know" of Epstein's sexual abuse of women and girls. He also confirmed the existence of hard drives held by Epstein's estate.

item.title: Martial arts star Chuck Norris dies at 86
item.summary: Norris karate chopped and kickboxed his way through more than a dozen action films, before leaping to TV in Walker, Texas Ranger.

item.title: Watch: Mitski performs a heavenly set from 'Nothing's About to Happen to Me'
item.summary: Plus, Mitski sits down with World Cafe's Raina Douris for a deep dive into her eighth studio album.
